# S312 — Spec questions: print every open question at once and take all answers in one call

**Findings:**  · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**2026-11-11** — Evidence 2026-11-11 (S223, run ork-20261111-024142-12c2): the orchestrator piped an answer into the one-at-a-time stdin prompt without reading the question. A Check-line question was answered 'runnable' where the standing rule (adj 263) says 'orchestrator', and the spec's Check lines were rewritten. Answering by decision key (--answer KEY=N) would have refused or shown the mismatch. Suggest moving this slice to v1.1.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

*Proposed.* `ork run P ID` and `ork wave start` stop the item with "needs N answers" and ask them one at a time on standard input. A session without a terminal sees only the first question: `askSpecQuestions` (`internal/cli/wave.go:312-360`) prints question 1, reads an empty line or end of input, and holds the item back, so questions 2 to N are never shown. On 2026-11-08 and 11-09 (S217: 4 questions, S243: 2, S244: 3, S310: 2) I had to read the others out of `~/.local/state/ork/spec-checks/*/spec-check.md` by hand, then pipe the answers in as `printf '2\n1\n' | ork run ...` in question order. That works but is fragile: a changed order, an added question or a stray newline gives wrong answers with no check.

What this slice adds: show all questions in one pass, and take answers by number or key in one call.

- `ork run P ID --questions` runs only the spec check and prints every open question (the same text the prompt shows, numbered, with each decision key), then exits with a distinct code (see `ork wait`'s exit codes in S257) and starts nothing.
- `ork run P ID --answer KEY=N` (repeatable; `KEY=text` for a free-text answer) answers by decision key and not by position. A question with no key is addressed as `#N`. A key that matches no open question, or a number outside the options, is refused before anything starts. All questions must be answered or the item is held back with the missing keys listed.
- `--json` prints the questions and the accepted answers as data.
- The interactive prompt is unchanged.

Open questions (owner answers before the relay starts):
- Q1 flag shape. (a) `--questions` and repeatable `--answer KEY=N` (recommended). (b) `--answers 1,2,1` by position only (shorter, fragile). (c) both.
- Q2 does `--questions` leave a record. (a) no, read only (recommended; the spec check result is cached already). (b) hold the item as today.

## Failing tests

- With a slice that has 3 open questions, `ork run P ID --questions` prints all three, each with its number, options, recommendation and decision key, writes nothing to the project, starts no run, and exits with the "questions pending" code.
- `ork run P ID --answer k1=2 --answer k2=1 --answer k3=1 --yes` records the three answers (the Owner decisions paragraph names each key) and starts the run, in any flag order.
- Missing an answer: the item is held back, nothing is recorded, and the message lists the unanswered keys.
- An unknown key, a number out of range, and a duplicate key are each refused with the key named, before any answer is recorded.
- `KEY=text` records the text as a free answer; an empty value is refused.
- `--json` prints `{questions:[...], answered:[...]}`.
- The one-at-a-time prompt, the piped-input path and the golden CLI text of the existing prompt are unchanged.

## Implement

1. Split `askSpecQuestions` into a printer (all questions) and the existing reader.
2. Add `--questions` and `--answer` to `ork run` and `ork wave start`, parsed beside `--yes`; reject `--answer` without questions pending, and `--questions` with `--yes`.
3. Map answers by key (or `#N`) to the question list before calling the existing answer path (`RecordSpecAnswers`), so one code path records them.
4. Exit codes follow S257 when it has landed; until then use ExitHeld and say so in the docs.
5. Docs and CHANGELOG, marked *proposed*.

Owner decisions (2026-11-09, accepted the recommended answers): flag shape -> (a) `--questions` and repeatable `--answer KEY=N` (recommended) [specs.questions-flag-shape, adj 224]. does `--questions` leave a record -> (a) no, read only (recommended; the spec check result is cached already) [specs.questions-record, adj 225].

Owner decisions (2026-11-11): How does `ork wave start` address answers when several items have questions? -> item prefix: `--answer ITEM:KEY=N` and `ITEM:#N` on `ork wave start`. `ork run` keeps `KEY=N` and `#N`, since it has one item. [specs.questions-wave-addressing]. What does each entry of `answered` hold in the `--json` output? -> key and answer: `answered` entries are `{item, key, answer}`. `key` is `#N` for a keyless question, and `answer` is the recorded "Label: summary" or free text. `questions` reuses `engine.SpecQuestion` (`ask`, `key`, `text`). [specs.questions-json-shape].
